what: Recipe 1: Diagnosing a deliberately-broken Bioconductor install
title: buildwright cookbook
text: common Bioconductor failure mode: lockfile pins Bioconductor package omits one Bioconductor dependencies (example dependency present transitively environment lock captured ). install dies part-way opaque “package ‘X’ available” error. buildwright surfaces install runs. build tiny broken renv.lock inline, write temp file, scan . S4Vectors requires IRanges, IRanges absent lockfile. also include RCurl, carries known system requirement (libcurl), diagnosis demonstrates system-library warning. Scan confirm sources read correctly (two Bioconductor, two CRAN): detect_conflicts() flags missing Bioconductor dependency. IRanges required S4Vectors absent scanned set, reported missing unsatisfiable: simulate_install() predicts consequence: IRanges install step (set), everything depends transitively blocked, plan feasible: Finally, check_sysreqs() (host system libraries) catches libcurl requirement RCurl pulls : single diagnose() call bundles ; print method gives --glance health summary gate install :
code: broken_lock <- '{   "R": { "Version": "4.3.2" },   "Bioconductor": { "Version": "3.18" },   "Packages": {     "BiocGenerics": {       "Package": "BiocGenerics",       "Version": "0.48.1",       "Source": "Bioconductor",       "Repository": "Bioconductor 3.18",       "Requirements": []     },     "S4Vectors": {       "Package": "S4Vectors",       "Version": "0.40.2",       "Source": "Bioconductor",       "Repository": "Bioconductor 3.18",       "Requirements": ["BiocGenerics", "IRanges"]     },     "RCurl": {       "Package": "RCurl",       "Version": "1.98-1.14",       "Source": "Repository",       "Repository": "CRAN",       "Requirements": ["bitops"]     },     "bitops": {       "Package": "bitops",       "Version": "1.0-7",       "Source": "Repository",       "Repository": "CRAN",       "Requirements": []     }   } }'  lock_path <- tempfile("broken-bioc-", fileext = ".lock") writeLines(broken_lock, lock_path) lib <- scan_library(lock_path) lib[, c("package", "version", "source")] #>  #> ── buildwright library scan ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> 4 packages from lockfile /tmp/RtmppHuZ7a/broken-bioc-1e797d4eb93.lock #> R version: "4.3.2" #> Bioconductor: "3.18" #> Sources: Bioconductor (2), CRAN (2) #>  #> # A tibble: 4 × 3 #>   package      version   source       #>   <chr>        <chr>     <chr>        #> 1 BiocGenerics 0.48.1    Bioconductor #> 2 bitops       1.0-7     CRAN         #> 3 RCurl        1.98-1.14 CRAN         #> 4 S4Vectors    0.40.2    Bioconductor table(lib$source) #>  #> Bioconductor         CRAN  #>            2            2 conf <- detect_conflicts(lib) conf[, c("package", "type", "satisfiable", "detail")] #>  #> ── buildwright conflicts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ! 1 issue: missing (1) #> • missing -- 'IRanges' is required by S4Vectors but is not present in the #> scanned set. plan <- simulate_install(lock_path, platform = "linux", host_libraries = character()) plan$feasible #> [1] FALSE plan$predicted_failures[, c("package", "predicted_status", "reason")] #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   package   predicted_status reason             #>   <chr>     <chr>            <chr>              #> 1 S4Vectors blocked          blocked by IRanges sr <- check_sysreqs(lib, platform = "linux", host_libraries = character()) sr[, c("package", "system_requirement", "status", "install_hint")] #>  #> ── buildwright system requirements (linux) ───────────────────────────────────── #> 1 requirement: 0 ok, 1 missing, 0 unknown #>  #> ── Likely-missing libraries ── #>  #> • cURL (for RCurl): apt-get install -y libcurl4-openssl-dev (or dnf install #> libcurl-devel) diag <- diagnose(lock_path, platform = "linux", host_libraries = character()) diag #>  #> ── buildwright diagnosis ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Input: /tmp/RtmppHuZ7a/broken-bioc-1e797d4eb93.lock (lockfile) #> 4 packages, platform "linux" #>  #> ! Conflicts: 1 (missing) #> ! System requirements: 1 likely-missing library #> ✖ Install simulation: 1 package predicted to fail/block #>  #> Inspect $library, $graph, $conflicts, $sysreqs, $plan; or report(x). summary(diag) #> # A tibble: 5 × 2 #>   metric             value #>   <chr>              <chr> #> 1 packages           4     #> 2 conflicts          1     #> 3 missing_sysreqs    1     #> 4 predicted_failures 1     #> 5 feasible           FALSE

what: Recipe 2: Auditing a real renv.lock from a public R project
title: buildwright cookbook
text: buildwright ships real lockfile taken rstudio/renv test resources (tests/testthat/resources/bioconductor.lock). genuine, small, Bioconductor environment contains two real reproducibility smells worth catching review. source breakdown shows first finding immediately: alongside two Bioconductor packages package installed Local source. Finding 1 – Local-source package. renv recorded Source: "Local" pointing path lock author’s machine (~/r/pkg/renv). Local source reproducible machine: repository commit restore . review flag ask CRAN pinned-GitHub version instead. Finding 2 – Bioconductor release mismatch. Bioconductor packages report source, lockfile pins different Bioconductor release branches. git_branch fields surfaced scan tibble, read raw lock JSON jsonlite expose : BiocGenerics pinned RELEASE_3_13 limma pinned RELEASE_3_14 – two different Bioconductor releases one environment. lockfile’s declared Bioconductor$Version 3.13, limma pin inconsistent environment claims describe. exactly sort drift makes Bioconductor restore fail silently mix releases. structural diagnosis clean (three packages missing dependencies cycles), point: lockfile can pass structural checks still carry reproducibility problems human see. wanted fetch lock live GitHub instead using bundled copy, following (run , since vignette must build offline):
code: real_lock <- system.file("extdata", "public-project.lock", package = "buildwright") rlib <- scan_library(real_lock) rlib[, c("package", "version", "source", "repository")] #>  #> ── buildwright library scan ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> 3 packages from lockfile #> /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/buildwright/extdata/public-project.lock #> R version: "4.1.2" #> Bioconductor: "3.13" #> Sources: Bioconductor (2), local (1) #>  #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   package      version   source       repository                                 #>   <chr>        <chr>     <chr>        <chr>                                      #> 1 BiocGenerics 0.38.0    Bioconductor https://git.bioconductor.org/packages/Bio… #> 2 limma        3.50.0    Bioconductor https://git.bioconductor.org/packages/lim… #> 3 renv         0.14.0-69 local        ~/r/pkg/renv table(rlib$source) #>  #> Bioconductor        local  #>            2            1 rlib[rlib$source == "local", c("package", "version", "repository")] #>  #> ── buildwright library scan ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> 1 packages from lockfile #> /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/buildwright/extdata/public-project.lock #> R version: "4.1.2" #> Bioconductor: "3.13" #>  #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   package version   repository   #>   <chr>   <chr>     <chr>        #> 1 renv    0.14.0-69 ~/r/pkg/renv raw <- jsonlite::fromJSON(real_lock, simplifyVector = FALSE) bioc <- Filter(function(p) identical(p$Source, "Bioconductor"), raw$Packages) branch_of <- function(p) if (is.null(p$git_branch)) NA_character_ else p$git_branch data.frame(   package = vapply(bioc, function(p) p$Package, character(1)),   version = vapply(bioc, function(p) p$Version, character(1)),   git_branch = vapply(bioc, branch_of, character(1)),   row.names = NULL ) #>        package version   git_branch #> 1 BiocGenerics  0.38.0 RELEASE_3_13 #> 2        limma  3.50.0 RELEASE_3_14 diagnose(real_lock) #>  #> ── buildwright diagnosis ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Input: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/buildwright/extdata/public-project.lock #> (lockfile) #> 3 packages, platform "linux" #>  #> ✔ Conflicts: none #> ✔ System requirements: no missing libraries detected #> ✔ Install simulation: feasible (0 warnings) #>  #> Inspect $library, $graph, $conflicts, $sysreqs, $plan; or report(x). url <- paste0(   "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/renv/main/",   "tests/testthat/resources/bioconductor.lock" ) dest <- tempfile("public-", fileext = ".lock") download.file(url, dest, quiet = TRUE) diagnose(dest)

what: Recipe 3: Catching a version-drift conflict between two CRAN packages
title: buildwright cookbook
text: Lockfiles often omit version constraints, installed libraries (many internal package sets) carry DESCRIPTION. two packages demand incompatible version ranges shared dependency, single version can satisfy install doomed. buildwright detects DESCRIPTION files directly. construct tiny three-package library temp directory: pkgA imports shared (>= 2.0), pkgB imports shared (<= 1.0), shared present 1.5. two ranges intersect. Scan directory installed library detect conflicts. shared dependency flagged version_conflict: intersection >= 2.0 <= 1.0 empty. constraints column records demands reviewer can see exactly packages disagree: simulate_install() marks shared failing (unsatisfiable constraints) pkgA/pkgB blocked behind :
code: lib_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "drift-lib") dir.create(lib_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)  write_desc <- function(name, version, imports = NULL) {   pkg_dir <- file.path(lib_dir, name)   dir.create(pkg_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)   lines <- c(     paste0("Package: ", name),     paste0("Version: ", version),     "Title: Fixture",     "Description: Fixture package for the buildwright cookbook.",     "License: GPL-3"   )   if (!is.null(imports)) lines <- c(lines, paste0("Imports: ", imports))   writeLines(lines, file.path(pkg_dir, "DESCRIPTION")) }  write_desc("pkgA", "1.0.0", imports = "shared (>= 2.0)") write_desc("pkgB", "1.0.0", imports = "shared (<= 1.0)") write_desc("shared", "1.5.0") drift_lib <- scan_library(lib_dir) drift_lib[, c("package", "version", "source", "requirements")] #>  #> ── buildwright library scan ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> 3 packages from library /tmp/RtmppHuZ7a/drift-lib #> R version: "4.6.0" #> Sources: local (3) #>  #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   package version source requirements #>   <chr>   <chr>   <chr>  <list>       #> 1 pkgA    1.0.0   local  <chr [1]>    #> 2 pkgB    1.0.0   local  <chr [1]>    #> 3 shared  1.5.0   local  <chr [0]>  dconf <- detect_conflicts(drift_lib) dconf[, c("package", "type", "constraints", "installed_version", "satisfiable")] #>  #> ── buildwright conflicts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ! 1 issue: version_conflict (1) #> Warning: Unknown or uninitialised column: `detail`. #> • version_conflict -- dconf$detail #> [1] "No single version of 'shared' satisfies all of: >= 2.0 (pkgA); <= 1.0 (pkgB)." dplan <- simulate_install(drift_lib) dplan$feasible #> [1] FALSE dplan$predicted_failures[, c("package", "predicted_status", "reason")] #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   package predicted_status reason                            #>   <chr>   <chr>            <chr>                             #> 1 shared  fail             unsatisfiable version constraints #> 2 pkgB    blocked          blocked by shared                 #> 3 pkgA    blocked          blocked by shared

what: Recipe 4: Wiring buildwright into renv / pak
title: buildwright cookbook
text: point fail fast early, install spends ten minutes compiling dies. bw_preinstall_check() gate: run front renv::restore() pak install , strict = TRUE, aborts problems predicted. healthy lockfile strict check passes silently install proceeds: broken lockfile, strict = TRUE raises error – script CI job aborts package built. catch error show message: real restore script place gate immediately install call (shown eval = FALSE touches network library): gate works front pak. host know system libraries installed, pass system-requirement check deterministic: CI step, one-line Rscript invocation fails job (non-zero exit) lockfile unhealthy: See package’s cookbook/ folder full, network-enabled versions recipes 1-2 (rendering HTML reports downloading live lockfile) ready--drop-cookbook/hooks/preinstall-hook.R.
code: bw_preinstall_check(bw_example("clean.lock"), strict = TRUE, quiet = TRUE) tryCatch(   bw_preinstall_check(bw_example("conflicted.lock"), strict = TRUE, quiet = TRUE),   error = function(e) cat("gate tripped:", conditionMessage(e), "\n") ) #> gate tripped: buildwright pre-install check failed. #> ✖ 4 conflicts, 6 predicted install failures, 0 missing system libraries. #> ℹ Run `diagnose()` or `report()` for details, or set `strict = FALSE` to warn #>   only. # restore.R -- run before bringing an environment up to its lockfile. buildwright::bw_preinstall_check("renv.lock", strict = TRUE) renv::restore() buildwright::bw_preinstall_check(   "renv.lock",   strict = TRUE,   host_libraries = c("libcurl", "openssl") ) pak::pkg_install("local::.") Rscript -e 'buildwright::bw_preinstall_check("renv.lock", strict = TRUE)'

title: Getting started with buildwright
text: build_dep_graph() turns library directed igraph edge -> B means “requires B”. can ask cycles diamond (shared) dependencies – packages multiple others depend , exactly version conflicts tend arise. clean lockfile acyclic, bw_cycles() returns empty list. diamond dependencies, ordered many packages need , point highest-risk shared packages:
code: g <- build_dep_graph(lib) g #>  #> ── buildwright dependency graph ──────────────────────────────────────────────── #> 14 packages, 23 dependency edges #> 14 present / 0 referenced-but-missing #> ✔ Acyclic (a valid install order exists) #> 6 shared (diamond) dependencies  bw_cycles(g) #> list() diamonds <- bw_diamonds(g) head(diamonds[, c("package", "n_dependents")]) #> # A tibble: 6 × 2 #>   package   n_dependents #>   <chr>            <int> #> 1 cli                  4 #> 2 rlang                4 #> 3 glue                 3 #> 4 lifecycle            3 #> 5 fansi                2 #> 6 vctrs                2

title: Getting started with buildwright
text: detect_conflicts() returns zero-row tibble library healthy. clean fixture healthy: conflicted.lock fixture . surfaces four problems: missing dependency, hard version conflict, version drift, cycle. required_by column list column, convert string printing data.frame: Reading rows: zeta missing (needed alpha); rlang version_conflict (one package wants >= 1.1.0, another <= 0.4.12); cli version_drift (package wants >= 99.0.0 pinned cli 3.6.2); ouroboros/boros form cycle.
code: detect_conflicts(bw_example("clean.lock")) #>  #> ── buildwright conflicts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ No dependency conflicts detected. conf <- detect_conflicts(bw_example("conflicted.lock")) conf$required_by <- vapply(conf$required_by, paste, character(1), collapse = ", ") as.data.frame(conf[, c("package", "type", "required_by", "satisfiable")]) #>              package             type                  required_by satisfiable #> 1               zeta          missing                        alpha       FALSE #> 2              rlang version_conflict needsNewRlang, needsOldRlang       FALSE #> 3                cli    version_drift               wantsRecentCli        TRUE #> 4 boros -> ouroboros            cycle             boros, ouroboros       FALSE

title: Getting started with buildwright
text: check_sysreqs() maps packages OS libraries need given platform. Passing host_libraries character vector makes presence deterministic: library counts present appears vector. empty vector, nothing installed, every requirement reported missing: Supplying, say, host_libraries = c("libcurl", "openssl") flip matching rows status = "ok".
code: sys <- check_sysreqs(   bw_example("missing-sysreq.lock"),   platform = "linux",   host_libraries = character() ) as.data.frame(sys[, c("package", "system_requirement", "status")]) #>      package system_requirement  status #> 1    askpass            OpenSSL missing #> 2       curl               cURL missing #> 3     magick        ImageMagick missing #> 4    openssl            OpenSSL missing #> 5      rJava           Java JDK missing #> 6  RPostgres  PostgreSQL client missing #> 7         sf               GDAL missing #> 8         sf               GEOS missing #> 9         sf               PROJ missing #> 10     units           udunits2 missing #> 11        V8          V8 engine missing #> 12      xml2            libxml2 missing

title: Getting started with buildwright
text: simulate_install() produces dependency-first install order predicts outcome every package, propagating failures: anything depends (transitively) failing package marked blocked. feasible FALSE, predicted_failures lists package fail blocked along reason – alpha blocked missing zeta, rlang dependents tripped version conflict, ouroboros/boros cycle.
code: plan <- simulate_install(bw_example("conflicted.lock")) plan$feasible #> [1] FALSE  as.data.frame(plan$predicted_failures[, c("package", "predicted_status", "reason")]) #>         package predicted_status                            reason #> 1         alpha          blocked                   blocked by zeta #> 2         boros             fail             in a dependency cycle #> 3 needsNewRlang          blocked                  blocked by rlang #> 4 needsOldRlang          blocked                  blocked by rlang #> 5     ouroboros             fail             in a dependency cycle #> 6         rlang             fail unsatisfiable version constraints

title: Getting started with buildwright
text: diagnose() runs scan, graph, conflict, system-requirement install steps together bundles results. summary() method returns compact two-column health tibble: individual pieces available diag$library, diag$graph, diag$conflicts, diag$sysreqs diag$plan. diagnosis (path/library) can also produce shareable artifact. report(x, format = "quarto") renders self-contained HTML report returns path, run_dashboard(x) launches interactive Shiny dashboard. omitted render open browser; call interactive session:
code: diag <- diagnose(   bw_example("conflicted.lock"),   platform = "linux",   host_libraries = character() ) summary(diag) #> # A tibble: 5 × 2 #>   metric             value #>   <chr>              <chr> #> 1 packages           9     #> 2 conflicts          4     #> 3 missing_sysreqs    0     #> 4 predicted_failures 6     #> 5 feasible           FALSE # Renders inst/report to a standalone HTML file and returns the path report(bw_example("conflicted.lock"), format = "quarto")  # Launches the interactive Shiny dashboard run_dashboard(bw_example("conflicted.lock"))

title: Dependency-Health and Build-Failure Diagnostics for Managed R Environments
text: Dependency-health build-failure diagnostics managed R environments.  buildwright predicts dependency failures large, managed R package distributions install attempted. scans renv lockfiles installed libraries, constructs dependency graph, detects version conflicts cycles, maps packages system-library requirements, simulates full install sequence surface every blocked package advance. Results available static Quarto HTML report, interactive Shiny dashboard, fail-fast CI hook gates renv::restore() pak installs.

title: Dependency-Health and Build-Failure Diagnostics for Managed R Environments
text: Running 300-package internal distribution Posit Connect Posit Workbench operationally hard. single transitive version bump—buried four levels deep—one missing system library can break fresh install halfway , leaving half-configured environment wall opaque error messages. Common pain points: Late failure. missing system library (libgdal, libpq, V8) causes rgdal, RPostgres, V8 fail compile time, often discovered 20-minute install run. Unsatisfiable version ranges. Package requires rlang >= 1.1.0; package B coded rlang <= 0.4.12. constraints can sit undetected lockfile months. Cycle detection. Circular Imports entries internal packages quietly poison igraph’s topological sort, producing random install orderings fail non-deterministically. Bioconductor release mismatches. lockfile pinned Bioc 3.13 silently conflicts packages require Bioc 3.14 APIs. early warning. Neither renv::restore() pak::pkg_install() performs pre-flight dependency-satisfiability check; discover problems install. Audit fatigue. Platform engineers lightweight way run nightly dependency-health scan live lockfile receive structured diff something regresses. buildwright addresses single diagnose() call Quarto report can schedule Connect.

title: Detect unsatisfiable dependency constraints — detect_conflicts
text: Walks every declared requirement reports packages whose constraints jointly satisfied. Four kinds problem surfaced:

title: Detect unsatisfiable dependency constraints — detect_conflicts
code: detect_conflicts(x)

title: Detect unsatisfiable dependency constraints — detect_conflicts
text: x bw_library, bw_depgraph, path scan_library() accepts.

title: Detect unsatisfiable dependency constraints — detect_conflicts
text: tibble class bw_conflicts, one row per problem, columns package, type, required_by (list column), constraints, installed_version, satisfiable, detail. healthy library yields zero-row tibble.

title: Detect unsatisfiable dependency constraints — detect_conflicts
text: missing – required package absent scanned set base package, nothing can depend successfully. version_conflict – two packages demand version ranges dependency whose intersection empty (single version works). version_drift – feasible range exists, version actually present (pinned lockfile) falls outside . cycle – packages form dependency cycle, install order exists. Version-range checks need version-qualified requirements. Installed-library scans always carry (parsed DESCRIPTION); renv.lock scans carry lockfile records , plain lockfiles focuses missing dependencies, cycles diamonds.

code: detect_conflicts(bw_example("clean.lock")) #>  #> ── buildwright conflicts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ No dependency conflicts detected. detect_conflicts(bw_example("conflicted.lock")) #>  #> ── buildwright conflicts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ! 4 issues: missing (1), version_conflict (1), version_drift (1), cycle (1) #> • missing -- 'zeta' is required by alpha but is not present in the scanned set. #> • version_conflict -- No single version of 'rlang' satisfies all of: >= 1.1.0 #> (needsNewRlang); <= 0.4.12 (needsOldRlang). #> • version_drift -- 'cli' 3.6.2 does not satisfy required range [>= 99.0.0] #> (from wantsRecentCli). #> • cycle -- Dependency cycle: boros -> ouroboros -> boros.

text: Predicted statuses: ok – expected install. warn – system library looks missing, pinned version drifts feasible range; install may still work risky. fail – directly unsatisfiable (version conflict, cycle, hard dependency missing). blocked – depends, transitively, something fails.

title: buildwright 0.1.0
text: First release. scan_library() reads installed libraries renv.lock files tidy bw_library inventory canonical sources (CRAN / Bioconductor / GitHub / local / custom repositories). build_dep_graph() constructs igraph dependency DAG, bw_cycles() bw_diamonds() helpers. detect_conflicts() finds missing dependencies, unsatisfiable version ranges, version drift, cycles. check_sysreqs() maps packages system libraries flags likely-missing ones, offline knowledge base ([bw_sysreq_library_db()], [bw_sysreq_package_map()]) optional pak path. simulate_install() produces dependency-first install order predicts failures (including blocked--dependency propagation) install. diagnose() runs full pipeline; report() renders parameterised Quarto (R Markdown fallback) HTML report; run_dashboard() launches Shiny app. bw_preinstall_check() gates renv / pak installs fail-fast hook.
